title: Why Is ASML Stock Falling, and is it a Buying Opportunity?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc upgrades ASML to a buying opportunity after its fall from a $2,000 52-week high to about $1,420. ASML supplies TSMC, Intel, Micron and Samsung with lithography equipment that is at least one step ahead of the competition and supply-constrained — customers are waiting until 2028-2029 for product — and price increases roll in through 2028. Wall Street now expects EPS growth of 33% a year for several years, orders run out to 2030, the operating margin is a record 38.5% (up from 25% in 2017) and cash flow from operations to sales is 57%. Despite booming sales and sold-out prospects, the stock trades at a forward P/E of 22.5, a relative discount he attributes to growing scepticism about the AI industry. He notes manufacturing facilities are welcomed by local communities for the jobs they bring, unlike data centres, though a data-centre slowdown could indirectly hit equipment demand. He revised his DCF valuation higher, with fair value very close to the $1,420 current price (the exact figure is garbled in the captions), and says an excellent business at a fair price is a great deal for long-term investors. He last evaluated ASML on 25 August, when it looked overvalued. He also offers free viewer voting on the next company he covers via a Google Form. Calls: ASML BUY at about $1,420 — FLIP from UNCERTAIN (19 Oct).
